# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

            throw new ClaimStatusException("Only a settle can be checked.");
        }
        String user = AuditUser.decode(userHeader);
        if (periods.isClosedOn(claim.getSheetId(), claim.getDueBy())) {
            throw new ClaimStatusException("A claim in a closed period cannot change status.");
        }
        String role = roles.roleOf(claim.getSheetId(), user);
        if (("open".equals(action) || "settle".equals(action) || "void".equals(action)) && !sheet.allows(action, role)) {
            throw new ClerkLimitException("A " + role + " cannot " + action + " a claim.");
        }

I read every file in scope. All 28 endpoint YAMLs run `GuardViewer` then `GuardArchived`, except the GETs and `unlock` (which has neither). No action runs `GuardClaimLock` except edit and add-line.

**Edit, add, quick-add, paste**
- **`ApplyClaim`** (PUT claim; steps: `ValidateClaim`, `TakeRollup`, `LoadClaim`, `GuardClaimLock`, then apply). Any viewer may edit; there is no role check.
  - Status must be DRAFT, else `InvalidClaimException`.
  - Refuses:
    - when the current `getDueBy()` is in a closed period;
    - when `amount` is not equal to `lines.totalOf`, if the claim has lines;
    - when the date changes and `holidays.dueBy(date, claim.getDueTerms())` is in a closed period;
    - when `person.retiredOn(date)`;
    - `checkCorrects`, then `checkRef`.
  - Sets amount, corrects, correctsDate, date, note, ref and tags, `lockedBy=null` and `editedBy`. It never changes `dueBy`.
  - Audit: `CLAIM_EDITED`.
  - Javadoc contradiction: it says "its person's terms on that date", but the code uses the stored `getDueTerms()`. The closed-period check is also hypothetical, because `dueBy` is never recomputed.
  - A blank date defaults to `sheet.getToday()`, but adding (`ClaimRules.make`) uses `entryDateInForce()`. `ValidateClaim`'s Javadoc also says "today". So add and edit disagree.
  - `grades` is injected but unused.
- **`BuildClaim`** only delegates to `ClaimRules.make`. Its Javadoc says the terms are "in force on its date", but `make` uses the terms on `created = sheet.getToday()`.
- **`ValidateClaim`** only delegates to `ClaimRules.check`.
- **Quick-add** (`ValidateQuickAdd`, `CheckQuickAddDate`, `FindOrAddPerson`, `BuildClaim`, `AuditClaimAdded`, `LogClaimStatus`, `AuditRollup`).
  - `ValidateQuickAdd` has its own `AMOUNT` regex `\d+(\.\d{1,2})?` (no negatives), separate from `ClaimRules`' `-?…`. Its Javadoc says "the sheet's today", but the claim is actually dated `entryDateInForce()`.

  - `FindOrAddPerson` matches by name or alias, ignoring case. It refuses a name used elsewhere in the tree (`tree.usedAround`). A new person gets the default grade.
  - It writes `PERSON_ADDED` plus rollup lines straight to the audit file, before `BuildClaim` runs. - **Paste** (`ValidatePaste`, then `AddPastedClaims`; no `TakeRollup`, it computes its own rollup).
  - `ValidatePaste` splits each line `split(",",4)`. A trailing ` #ref` in the note becomes the ref. It calls `ClaimRules.check` with no corrects and no tags, so a negative line is refused and tags are impossible.
  - Matching: same person, same date (blank means `entryDateInForce`), same trimmed note, against that person's claims before the paste, preferring a DRAFT.
    - A non-DRAFT match refuses the whole paste.
    - A matched DRAFT is refused if another user holds its lock. Its amount is edited only if it differs; the closed-period and line-total checks run only in that case. It gets `CLAIM_EDITED`.
    - The line's ref is ignored for a matched draft, and no retirement check is made.
  - Otherwise the claim is built by `make` and refs are de-duplicated within the paste. Its `CLAIM_ADDED`/`LATE_ENTRY` lines are inline copies of `ClaimRules.auditAdded`.

- **`ApplyDefer`**: checks the closed period first, then that the status is OPEN. `until` must be after `getToday()`. Sets `deferredUntil`. No role check. Audit: `CLAIM_DEFERRED … until=`.

- **`ApplyRedate`**: hard-coded steward. OPEN or PENDING. Refuses a closed due-by and a retired person. Changes only `date`; `dueBy`, number and binding are untouched.
  - It runs `lockSheet` plus `refresh` only under period numbering, even though it takes no number. This looks like leftover code.
  - Audit: `CLAIM_REDATED … old= new=`. No `LogClaimStatus`.
- **`ApplyReassign`**: permission comes from `sheet.allows("reassign", role)` and refusal throws `ClerkLimitException`. The YAML comment says "a steward".

  - If the claim has a number, it takes a new one keyed on `getDueBy()`: per-period `P:<name>` or `X`, else `takeNextInFiscalYear`.
  - It calls `bind(false,null)`, so it loses its stated figure, and `relist` makes it the person's newest.
  - Audit: `CLAIM_REASSIGNED … from= to=`. The person field is the new person.
  - Lock order: it calls `lockSheet(sheet)`, and `takeNextInFiscalYear` then calls `lockTree`, which locks the top sheet and then the sheet. `ApplySplit` locks the top first. That is an inverted lock order and a possible deadlock.
- **`ApplyResettle`**: checks the closed period first, then steward (`ClerkLimitException`), then that the status is SETTLED.
  - New `due = ClaimFigures(...).openDue(claim)`: today's rates and grades, unbound; null means n/a.
  - Runs `NotifyWatchers` and `LogClaimStatus`. The new SETTLED log line moves `settledOn` to today.
  - Audit: `CLAIM_RESETTLED … old= new=`.
- **`ApplySplit`**:
  - Amount regex `\d+(\.\d{1,2})?`, `setScale(2)`, must satisfy 0 < amount < `claim.amount`.
  - Permission: `sheet.allows("open", role)`, but a refusal throws `ClaimStatusException`, not `ClerkLimitException`.
  - Refuses a closed due-by. Locks the sheet under per-period numbering, else `lockTree`, then refreshes. Requires OPEN and not `isDeferredOn(today)`.
  - The original's amount is reduced and it is unbound.
  - The new OPEN claim gets the same date and note, the tags, `splitFrom` (the original's number), `openedBy`, and `fixDue(date, terms)` with terms taken on **today**. The Javadoc says "on the date". It gets `lateEntry` if the period is soft-closed. Ref, corrects and proofs are not copied.
  - Its numbering code is copy-pasted from `ApplyReassign`, keyed on the new `dueBy`.
  - Audit: `CLAIM_SPLIT … into=`, then the new claim's OPEN event.
- **Part-settle**: `CheckPartSettle` (byte-identical to `CheckClaimSettle`, both `run("settle",…, true)`), then `ApplySplit`, then `ApplyPartSettle` (`run(... false, true)` overload plus `ClaimRules.log`).

- **`ApplyRemind`**: OPEN or PENDING. Refused if already reminded on today. It escalates if `escalateAfter` is set, the claim is not yet escalated, it has a previous reminder, and calendar days since then are ≥ the gap.

  - Audit: `REMIND`, plus `ESCALATE`.
- **`ApplyProof`**: kind is receipt by default, or photo. Refused only for SETTLED or VOID, so DELETED and REJECTED claims can still gain proofs. No closed-period check.

**Editor and lines**
- **`ApplyLock`**: DRAFT only, then not in a closed period, then not `isLockedFor(by)`. Locking releases the user's other locks on the sheet. No audit.
  - The YAML says the lock also ends "when the sheet's today changes". Nothing in `claim/` does that.
- **`GuardClaimLock`** refuses only if another user holds the lock. An unlocked claim can be saved without ever locking it.
- **`ReleaseLock`** clears the lock only if the caller holds it. There are no archived or viewer guards.
- **`ValidateLine` / `ApplyLine`**:
  - Label must be non-empty. Qty must match `\d{1,9}` and be ≥ 1. Unit must match `\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,2})?`, `setScale(2)`.
  - DRAFT only, and not in a closed period. Saves the line dated today, sets `amount = lines.totalOf` (the sum of qty × unit, no rounding step) and `editedBy`.
  - Javadoc gap: it does not release the lock and does not check retirement.
  - Audit: `CLAIM_LINE_ADDED … label= qty= unit=`.
- **`ApplyComment`**: any status, text trimmed and non-empty. Audit: `COMMENT_ADDED … text=`.

**`ClaimRepository`**
- **`checkCorrects`**: the target must be a SETTLED claim of the same person with that number. remaining = target amount + the sheet's other corrections of it (VOID, DELETED and the claim being edited are excluded). Refuses if −amount > remaining. Returns the target's date.
- **`checkRef`**: case-insensitive, excludes the claim itself.
- **Numbering**: `takeNextInFiscalYear` uses `FY<year>-<n>`. The year comes from the due-by date and `fiscalStartMonth`, and the sequence is shared across the tree, held on the top sheet. `takeNextInSequence` is per sheet.
- `takeNextNumber`/`lastNumber` (the old integer numbering) have no callers.
- **`batchFor`**: locks the sheet and returns the same number for a key it has seen before.
- **`AuditBatchSettled`**: `BATCH_SETTLED batch= count= total=`. `count` includes claims in the batch of any status, but `total` sums only SETTLED claims with a non-null due. A key that matches nothing writes nothing.

**Logs and audit lines**
- `ClaimLog.line()` is `STATUS by U on D due=X|n/a`. `settledOn` and `deletedOn` take the latest matching line.
- `Tags.normalise`: trimmed, lower-case, de-duplicated, sorted, comma-joined, null if empty.
- `ClaimAudit.line`: `EVENT sheet= by= person= amount=(scale 2) date= [number=]`.

**Inconsistencies across actions**
- **Role checks**: three styles. A hard-coded `STEWARD` check (waive, redate, resettle), the permission matrix (reassign, split), and none (hold, defer, remind, proof, edit, line, comment). They also throw different exception types.
- **Closed-period checks**: missing from hold, waive, remind and proof. Where present, the order of checks varies (closed period before status in defer and resettle, after in others).
- **Rollup steps**: `TakeRollup`/`AuditRollup` are missing from remind, proof, comment and lock.
- **Duplicated code**:
  - the per-period/FY number-taking block (reassign, split, and probably `ApplyClaimStatus`);
  - the due-by and terms calculation (`make`, `ApplySplit`, `CheckQuickAddDate`);
  - the amount regex (three copies);
  - the closed-period, line-total and lock checks for an edit (`ApplyClaim`, paste, `ApplyLine`);
  - `CLAIM_ADDED` (paste copies `auditAdded`);
  - `NOTIFY` (`AuditPartSettle`).

**How tangled it felt:** quite tangled. Each rule is spread across a YAML step list, a Javadoc that often promises more than the code does, the shared helpers `ApplyClaimStatus.run` (more than 15 parameters, boolean flags, overloads) and `ClaimRules`, and copy-pasted blocks. To know whether an action is guarded you have to read the YAML and the Java together. Wording like "as the X button does" stands in for actual shared code in several places.

content.text: One of the three helper agents has reported back (on claim actions). Two are still running: one on people, roles and the sheet, one on periods, statements, pools and rates. I'll write the full answer when both are in.

All of this was read-only; I changed no files. Everything below is under `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610241-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`. Every write pipeline starts with `GuardViewer` (a viewer is refused) and `GuardArchived`, so I only mention a role check when it goes beyond that.

**period/**
- **Adding (`ValidatePeriod`, `ApplyPeriod`)**: the name is trimmed and required; from and to must be calendar dates with to ≥ from; `cap` is blank or a whole number of 1 or more. Refused if the name is already used on the sheet (case-sensitive) or the dates overlap another period (both ends inclusive). Audit: `PERIOD_ADDED ... period= from= to= [cap=]`.
- **`ClosePeriod.totals`**: every listed person starts at 0.00. A claim is added in when `ClaimFigures.countsAsOf(c, statusAt(toDate), person, sheet.getToday())` and `period.contains(c.getDueBy())`. The status is taken from `ClaimLogRepository.statusesOn(sheet, toDate)`, but the amount is `ClaimFigures.due(c)` as it stands now (current rates, grades, late charge). n/a is skipped and the result is scaled to 2. So the status is historical but the money is current.
- **`ClosePeriod.carried`**: takes claims whose due-by falls in an *earlier* period (its to-date is before this period's from-date) and whose status at this period's to-date was OPEN or PENDING and that pass `countsAsOf`. It sums their current `due`, then adds `period.openingOf(id)`. A claim whose due-by is in no period is never carried.
- **Freezing**: `Period.close` and `Period.softClose` → `fix` freezes `personTotals` and `personCarried`, and `closedTotal` = the sum of `personTotals`. `reopen()` clears all of these but keeps `personOpening`.
- **Who may, and what is refused**:
  - Close: `sheet.allows("close", role)`; refused if already closed. A soft-closed period can be closed, which re-fixes it. Audit `PERIOD_CLOSED ... period= total=`.
  - Soft-close: uses the same "close" permission; refused if closed or soft-closed. Audit `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED ... total=`.
  - Lock and unlock: hard-coded `Role.STEWARD`, not the permission matrix. Audit `PERIOD_LOCKED` / `PERIOD_UNLOCKED`.
  - Reopen: `sheet.allows("reopen", role)`; refused if locked or not closed. Audit `PERIOD_REOPENED`.
- **`AutoClosePeriods`** runs in the today.PUT pipeline after `ApplyToday`, only when `graceDays` is set. It closes each period that is not closed or soft-closed and where `toDate + grace` is before the new today, in to-date then id order. It skips the permission check and calls `history.recordOn(period, toDate)`; a manual close does not. Audit `PERIOD_CLOSED ... total= auto=yes`.
- **`isClosedOn` / `isSoftClosedOn`** test the claim's **due-by** (not its date). Closed blocks add, status change, lock, line, reassign, split, resettle, defer, redate, paste and quick-add. Soft-closed only sets `lateEntry` (in `ClaimRules` and `ApplySplit`).
- **Period cap**: enforced only in `ApplyClaimStatus`, on "open" or "review". It takes the first period with a cap that contains the claim's due-by, counts the person's *other* claims currently OPEN or PENDING with due-by in that period, and refuses when the count is ≥ cap. It uses current status, not historical.
- **Generating periods**:
  - `GeneratePeriods`: blank dates default to the sheet's today. It makes one period per month named `yyyy-MM`, silently skipping a month whose name exists or that overlaps.
  - `GenerateQuarters`: periods named `yyyy-Q1..Q4`.
  - `GenerateFiscalYear`: 12 months starting at `sheet.getFiscalStartMonth()`, reusing `GeneratePeriods.months`.
  - None of them set a cap. All audit as `PERIOD_ADDED` (via `AuditPeriodsGenerated`, with no cap field).
- **Javadoc problems**:
  - In `Period.java`, the Javadoc "due-total fixed when closed" sits on the `cap` field, and `closedTotal` has none.
  - `ClosePeriod`'s Javadoc says "(by the standing rule, clerk and steward may)", but that is the permission matrix's default, not code.
  - `SoftClosePeriod`'s refusal message says "already closed" even for a soft-closed period.

**statement/**
- **`TakeStatement`, live (no asOf)**: `dueTotal = figures.dueTotal(mine, today, person)`. Each claim with `countsLive` gets `bind(true, due(claim))`; every other claim gets `bind(false, null)`. It records a `BindingLog` (madeOn = the sheet's today, holding each bound claim and its figure) and a `Statement` (takenOn = asOf or today, madeOn = today, `claims` = the count).
- **`TakeStatement`, asOf**: refused if not a calendar date, if after today, or if before `person.getAddedOn()`. It rebuilds the state at that date:

I read every file in your scope, plus the pipeline YAMLs to see which guards run before each step. All of it is read-only. The biggest findings: any clerk can make themselves steward, a person's hold never takes a claim out of any figure (Person.java's Javadoc says it does), and a transfer that ends in a merge does not behave like a merge.

**Every change step.** Each change pipeline starts with `GuardViewer` (refuses a viewer with "A viewer cannot change anything", HTTP 403), then `GuardArchived`. Pipelines that move figures wrap the work in `TakeRollup` … `AuditRollup`, which writes `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS`/`ALERT` lines.

**person/**
- **Retire / unretire**
  - `retiredFrom` set (even a future date) counts as retired at once for merge and transfer refusals.
  - `retiredOn(date)` is strict: the claim date must be *after* `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement. It refuses new claims, redates and reassigns.
  - `retiredBy(today)` is inclusive: from that day, unbound OPEN and PENDING claims leave the live totals.
  - `ApplyRetire` (date or the sheet's today, stores `retiredMadeOn`) has **no role check and no "already retired" refusal**. Retiring again overwrites `retiredFrom` and the earlier retirement is lost.
  - `ApplyUnretire` refuses "Only a retired person can be unretired"; it pushes a `PersonRetirement(from, today)`.
  - Audit: `PERSON_RETIRED … name from=`, `PERSON_UNRETIRED … name on=`.
- **Hold** (`ApplyHold`): from defaults to today, to is open-ended; refuses a to-date before the from-date; anyone non-viewer may. Audit `PERSON_HELD … name from=` has no `to=`.
  - **Contradiction:** Person.java's Javadoc on `holds` says held OPEN/PENDING claims "count in no live total". `ClaimFigures` and `Rollup`'s Javadoc say a hold takes no claim out of any figure, and the code does that. `heldOn()` is used only by `pool/RespondWithPools` (zero cut).
- **Flag** (`ApplyFlag`): steward only (`roleOf`, so delegation counts); reason required; until defaults to today, inclusive (`flaggedOn`). The reason is shown only while in force. A flag is never cleared, only replaced. Effect: `ApplyClaimStatus` refuses "open" on a flagged person's claim for a non-steward. Audit `PERSON_FLAGGED … name reason until`.
- **Approver** (`ApplyApprover`): no role check, and the user name is not checked against anything; blank means none. `ApplyClaimStatus:195` lets the approver approve or reject PENDING claims. Audit `APPROVER_SET … name user=`.
- **Edit** (`ApplyPerson`): `@Version` conflict gives `PersonConflictException`; name, alias, tree (`TreeNames`) and contact uniqueness are checked.
  - Grade: recorded as a `PersonGrade` from `gradeFrom`, or today when blank. An undated grade equal to the one in force today is not recorded. A dated one is always recorded.
  - Terms: blank from-date with the value already in force today means no change; otherwise `setTerms`, or `setTermsFrom` when a from-date is given.
  - Editing a retired person is not refused.
  - Audit `PERSON_EDITED … name grade [terms=] [contact=]`.
- **Merge** (`ApplyMerge`): steward only (`ClerkLimitException`). Refuses merging into themselves, or either person retired. Moves claims (relisted as newest), plans, patrons (both directions, no self or repeats), pool shares (added together), crews led and crew memberships, statements (placed before the other's) and the binding log. Name and aliases become aliases. Watchers and dated grades are dropped. Closed periods and flags are not checked. Audit `PERSON_MERGED … from into`.
- **Transfer** (`ApplyTransfer`)
  - Steward on the *source* sheet only; the user's role on the target is never checked.
  - Refuses: own sheet, retired, archived target, retired match on the target, contact clash (only when not merging). A missing target sheet is created. `TreeNames` is not checked on the target.
  - Copies claims (new ids, frozen dues, `bind(stated, statedDue)`, logs, comments, lines) and renumbers them on the target.
  - **Contradiction:** the Javadoc says a transfer that finds a matching name merges "exactly as a merge does". In code, patrons, pool memberships and crew memberships are *dropped* and led crews lose their lead. `ApplyMerge` moves all of these.
  - Audit `PERSON_TRANSFERRED sheet=from … to=`, rollup lines, `PERSON_TRANSFERRED sheet=to … from=`, optional `PERSON_MERGED`, rollup lines.
- **Undo transfer** (`ValidateTransferUndo`, then `ApplyTransfer` back): steward only; needs `originSheet` and `arrivedOn`, and only on the day of arrival (`arrivedOn == today`). It is not a real undo: holds, patrons and so on are not restored.
  - `AuditTransferUndone` writes `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE … to=` and then the same sheet's rollup lines again, so they appear twice.
- **Move** (`ApplyMove`): swaps `position` with the neighbour; refuses top-up and bottom-down. Audit `PERSON_MOVED … position=` (1-based).
- **Patron** (`ApplyPatron`): refuses self or a repeat; cycles (A→B, B→A) are allowed; retired people allowed. `PATRON_ADDED`.
- **Alias** (`ApplyAlias`): refuses any name or alias on the sheet or its tree, ignoring case. `PERSON_ALIAS_ADDED`.
- **Grades and snapshots:** `PersonGrades.on(date)` gives the latest dated grade on or before the date, else `first`; a null date gives `first`. `asOf` filters by `madeOn`. A `PersonSnapshot(takenOn, dueTotal)` is appended only by `AuditSnapshot`.
- **`Person.asOf`** (used only by `TakeStatement`): ignores `datedTerms`, and copies the *current* flag and approver whatever the date.

**role/**
- `roleOf` returns steward if the user's own role isn't steward and a `Delegation` covers the sheet's today (latest by id). Otherwise it returns the stored role, default clerk.
  - A *viewer* who is delegated becomes a steward and passes `GuardViewer`.
  - A delegation stays in force after the delegator is demoted.
- **`ApplyRole` has no role check: any clerk can make themselves steward.** Roles are clerk, steward or viewer. `ROLE_SET … user role`.

Nothing was changed. I read the core calculation code, the claim status rules and the front end myself; three helper agents read the rest of the Java back end. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## Where the numbers come from Nearly every money figure on the screen is calculated **in the browser**. The server sends plain claims, people, rates and settings, and the front end works out every due and total from them. The server has its own copy of the same rules in `claim/ClaimFigures.java`. It uses that copy when it freezes a figure: when a claim is settled, re-settled or part-settled, when a statement is taken, when a period is closed, and for the rollup, snapshot and alert audit lines. | Server | Browser | |---|---| | `ClaimFigures.due` / `figure` / `lateCharge` / `floored` / `rounding` / `lateFrom` / `overdue` | `rates.ts`: `chargedOf` / `figureOf` / `dueOf` / `atLeast` / `roundsHalfUp`; `claims.ts`: `lateFromOf` / `isOverdue` | | `ClaimFigures.counts` / `countsLive` / `countsClaimed` / `countsAsOf` | `claims.ts`: `counts` / `countsLive` / `countsClaimed` / `countsAsOf` | | `ClaimFigures.dueTotal` (with the cap) | `rates/due.slot.tsx`: `personDue` / `personExcess` / `personFigures` | | `ClaimFigures.rateOn`, `Rate.forClaim` | `rates.ts`: `rateOn` / `rateForClaim` | | `Sheet.floorOn`, `latePctOn`, `roundingOn`, … | `roles.ts`: `settingOn` | ## Shown on each claim row (`claims/list.slot.tsx`) - **claim-due** comes from `chargedOf` (server: `ClaimFigures.due`). It is taken from the first of these that applies: 1. **Frozen due** (`Claim.due`): set when the claim is settled. 2. **Bound figure** (`statedDue`): while the claim is bound by its person's last statement. 3. **Live figure**, worked out in four steps: - **Base:** amount × the rate percent ÷ 100. - The rate is for the grade the person had on the claim's date (`PersonGrades.on`), in force on that date. - It is looked up on this sheet first, then up the parent chain (`findInChain`: up to 3 parent levels, then the sheet it was cloned from). - If that rate's to-date is already past, there is none (`Rate.endedBy`). - A rate saved as forward-only (from-date on or after the sheet's today) does not apply to claims that existed before it (`Rate.forClaim` / `rateForClaim`). - With no rate, the due shows **n/a**. - **Rounding** to 2 decimals (`ClaimFigures.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`): - If a `rounding` setting is in force on the claim's rounding date (`roundsOn`), it decides. - Otherwise the claim rounds half-up when dated before `policyDateInForce` (the policy date, or the sheet's today when blank), and half-to-even on or after it. - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`correctsDate`). - **Floor:** the figure is raised to `floorOn(claim date)`, which defaults to 1.00. Corrections take no floor. - **Late charge** (`chargeByBoundary`): - For each full 30 days since `lateFrom` (the due-by plus the `grace-` days in force on the claim's date), it adds `latePctOn(boundary date)` × (floored figure + charges so far), rounded like the due. So it compounds. - There is none for a correction, a `waived` claim, or a claim that is not overdue. - **claim-overdue:** the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `lateFrom` is before the sheet's today. - **claim-due-by:** `fixDue` sets it when the claim is created: the `dueTerms`-th business day after `dueFrom`, skipping weekends and holidays (`BusinessDays.after`). - `dueTerms` is the person's own terms, else their grade's terms, else the sheet's (default 14). All are taken as in force on the sheet's today at creation (`Sheet.termsFor`). - Re-dating or editing the claim never changes it. Adding a holiday reworks it (`reworkDueBy`) on every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID. - **claim-period:** the period that contains the **due-by**, not the claim's date. - **claim-number:** given when the claim is opened (`ApplyClaimStatus`). - Normally `FY-`: the year is the fiscal year of the due-by, and the count is shared across the sheet's tree. - While `periodNumberingOn`, it is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by is in no period. - REVIEW claims get no number until a steward reviews them. Reassigning or splitting a claim gives it a new number. - **Other values shown on the row:** - status, stated, opened-by, corrects - deferred (the row's own `today < deferredUntil` test, which does not check that the claim is OPEN, unlike `isDeferred`) and deferred-until - proofs, receipts and photos - split-from, late-entry (added while the due-by's period was soft-closed), waived, held - reminded, ref, tags, batch - review-late (`reviewOn` plus `reviewSla` is before today) - lines, comments, log and timeline ## Shown on each person row - **person-due-total** (`personDue` / `ClaimFigures.dueTotal`): - Adds up the dues of the claims that pass `countsLive`: - OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED count; OPEN deferred past today does not. - Once the person's retirement date is reached, their unbound OPEN and PENDING claims drop out. - It is **n/a** when the person's grade today has no rate today, **unless** some counted claim keeps a figure: it is frozen, bound, live at another grade, or dated on or before today. - It is capped at `cap`, and **person-excess** shows the amount above the cap. - **person-claimed** (`sumOf` / `countsClaimed`): the sum of amounts, not dues. Corrections are left out. - **person-settled-total / person-open-total** (`splitOf`), **person-overdue-count / -total** (`overdueOf`), **person-aged-0-30 / 31-60 / 61** (by days since the claim's date), **person-active** (an OPEN or PENDING claim that counts, dated within the last 30 days). - **person-period-

-due-total / -carried** (`personPeriodDue` / `personPeriodCarried`): - Counted by the status each claim had at the end of the period (`statusOn` from the claim's status log), but valued at today's figure. - "Carried" covers claims whose due-by is in earlier periods and that were still OPEN or PENDING at that point, plus the person's opening balance. - Once the period is closed or soft-closed, the frozen `personTotals` / `personCarried` are shown instead. - **person-backing:** each patron's frozen dues on SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days, times the patron's equal share (`sharesOf`), rounded half-to-even. - **person-cut-total** (pool cuts: see Holds below). - **Statement and snapshot figures:** statement-count, stated-total and statement-date, statement lines and snapshot lines are all frozen values from the server. - **Other values:** - grade (`gradeOn` today), terms, retired and retired-from, retirement lines - hold and hold lines, flag (shown while `flaggedOn`), approver - aliases, clashing, origin, tags, watched, contact ## Sheet-level totals - **rollup-due-total / header-due-total** (`trimmedSum`): with three or more people, the highest and the lowest are left out. - **classic-due-total:** the same sum with nothing left out. - **Overdue, claimed, settled/open and aged totals.** - **Period due-totals** (`periodDue`), and **classic period totals**, which count each claim by its status now rather than at the period's end. - **Month and tag totals.** - **crew-due-total:** the lead's and members' `personDue` added up. - **Consolidated totals:** the sheet plus all its descendant sheets, each with its own today, rates and settings. - **Dashboard and header counters** (the dashboard is shown only to stewards). ## What freezes a figure, and when - **Settle** (`ApplyClaimStatus`) freezes `due` at `ClaimFigures.due`, including any late charge on that day. - With `?on=` it freezes the due as it stood at the end of that date, rebuilt through `AsOf`. - When the due is n/a it stays live. - **Re-settle** (steward only) replaces the frozen due with `openDue`: today's rates and grades, ignoring any statement binding. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds every claim that passes `countsLive` to its current due (`stated` and `statedDue`) and unbinds all the others. - A bound claim's due stops following the sheet's today. - Reassigning, splitting or cancelling a statement unbinds the claim. Cancelling does not restore the previous statement's bindings. - **Closing or soft-closing a period** freezes `personTotals`, `personCarried` and `closedTotal`.
